articles.headline: NBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Thunder remain title favorites heading into Game 7 vs. Spurs
articles.description: Game 7 is set for Saturday in Oklahoma City, with the Thunder-Spurs winner playing the Eastern Conference champion Knicks in the NBA Finals.

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [1296x729]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Victor Wembanyama are Nos. 1 and 2 in the Finals MVP odds, respectively.

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [608x342]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Thunder are back to being odds-on title favorites after taking a 3-2 series lead over the Spurs.
images.alt: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

images.name: Jalen Brunson [608x342]
images.caption: Jalen Brunson has the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson

images.caption: The Knicks are looking to end the series against the Cavaliers tonight, as they have the second-shortest title odds and are an overwhelming favorite to win the East.

images.caption: The Knicks are now heavy favorites to win the Eastern Conference after taking a 3-0 series lead over the Cavs.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson

article.headline: Kuzma has 32 points and 12 rebounds as Wizards end 9-game losing streak with rout of Pistons
article.description: - Kyle Kuzma had 32 points and 12 rebounds as the Washington Wizards ended a nine-game losing streak with a 126-107 rout of the Detroit Pistons on Monday in a battle of the NBA's worst teams.
article.linkText: Kuzma has 32 points and 12 rebounds as Wizards end 9-game losing streak with rout of Pistons

images.name: Cade Cunningham shows off vision with nice dime vs. Washington Wizards
images.caption: Cade Cunningham shows off vision with nice dime vs. Washington Wizards

article.story:
DETROIT -- - Kyle Kuzma had 32 points and 12 rebounds as the Washington Wizards ended a nine-game losing streak with a 126-107 rout of the Detroit Pistons on Monday in a battle of the NBA's worst teams.

"My childhood dream was about playing on this court," said Kuzma, who grew up about an hour north of Little Caesars Arena. "It's always good to get a chance to play at home in front of my friends and family."

Washington (3-14) won for the first time since a 132-116 victory over the Charlotte Hornets on Nov. 8.

The Pistons (2-15) have lost 14 straight after beating the Chicago Bulls 118-102 on Oct. 28.

"That wasn't fight on the floor," Pistons coach Monty Williams said in a brief postgame press conference. "That wasn't Pistons basketball by any stretch of the imagination. That's what this is -- we have to have people that honor the organization and the jersey by competing at a high level every night."

Kuzma, who spent the day before the game delivering charitable donations in his home city of Flint, added eight assists while committing two turnovers. Deni Avdija and Danilo Gallinari scored 16 for the Wizards.

Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 26 points and seven assists. Jalen Duren had 12 points and 14 rebounds as Detroit fell to 4-38 since last season's trade deadline.

"There are a lot of little things we can talk about, but we just didn't play hard," Isaiah Livers said. "Every team has roles, and it feels like none of us are playing our roles to the best of our abilities."

Tyus Jones scored eight points in the first five minutes of the third to put Washington up 71-63, and Kuzma took over at that point. He finished the quarter with 18 points and seven rebounds as the Wizards led by as many as 14.

Washington led 94-83 at the end of the quarter, then scored the first five points of the fourth. Detroit never got the deficit back to single digits.

The teams combined to hit just 24.2% (8-33) 3-pointers in the first half with the Pistons going 3-16 (18.8%).

UP NEXT

Wizards: At the Orlando Magic on Wednesday.

Pistons: Host the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday.
